clue.text: Say, shoots for mixing closely in paganism

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the word aloud and enter what it sounds like

parts.note: wicker is pliant twigs or shoots woven tightly together, as for baskets

explanation.surface: Someone describes young plant shoots being blended in a pagan rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals a homophone: WICKER, in a non-rhotic accent, is pronounced like the name of the modern pagan religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern revival of witchcraft and nature worship, a form of neo-paganism.

clue.text: PG being kicked out owed family

indicators.note: something kicked out of shape is knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone is evicted because their family owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: P G Wodehouse, comic novelist, is clued by his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelham Grenville Wodehouse wrote under the initials P G, creator of Jeeves.

clue.text: Doctor supports wine area offering a little comfort

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or wine-growing area in France
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor backs a vineyard region that offers some solace.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supports' puts the doctor below the wine area.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom a crumb of comfort means a small amount of consolation.

clue.text: One mariner or another, say, that's taking rope down

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is one sailor

indicators.note: say means the next word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: another mariner, a sailor

explanation.surface: Two sailors handle the rigging as one comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abseils descends a cliff by sliding down a rope.

clue.text: Like a goose, paid for following worldwide system

indicators.note: following places the payment word after the system word

parts.note: the Web is the worldwide system of linked internet pages
to foot a bill is to pay it, so paid for gives footed

explanation.surface: A goose-like entity pays its way after the internet takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese have toes joined by skin, so a goose is literally web-footed.

clue.text: Cart taking lover for execution

indicators.note: execution by beheading takes off the first letter

parts.note: a swain is a lover or suitor

explanation.surface: A cart takes a lover to the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' implies beheading, removing the head letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is an old word for a farm wagon or cart, as in Constable's Hay Wain.

clue.text: A kebab? Send out for veg too

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a takeaway kebab also asks for vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot beans in tomato sauce count as a vegetable, as well as a takeaway side.

clue.text: Should I rise to seize power, for best results?

indicators.note: to seize means the reversed phrase grips the power letter
rise in a down clue means the phrase is read upwards

parts.note: should I can be put as am I to, as in 'Am I to go?'

explanation.surface: An ambitious figure wonders whether to take power for the best outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns AMITO to OTIMA, and 'to seize' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima, plural of optimum, are the most favourable outcomes or conditions.

clue.text: Thieves found among the dregs

definitions.meaning: what remains at the bottom of a teacup

explanation.surface: Thieves are discovered among the lowest of society.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: tea leaf rhymes with thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns thieves into tea leaves, the sediment left in a cup.

clue.text: European fitting a gold shower delighted her

indicators.note: fitting means the European is fitted round the letter

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A European gets a golden shower, and she is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus visited the imprisoned princess as a shower of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus came to the Argive princess as golden rain, fathering Perseus.

clue.text: Traps second joint

parts.note: traps is a drummer's slang for a drum kit, so drums
a tick is a moment, informally a second

explanation.surface: A snare catches the second joint of a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' looks like a verb; it is a noun for a drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower leg of a cooked chicken is a joint of meat served at table.

clue.text: Following end of August, bad weather

indicators.note: end of takes only the closing letter of August

parts.note: rain is the classic bad weather

explanation.surface: Late summer brings a spell of nasty weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a retinue or body of followers attending someone important.

clue.text: Little creature in extremely popular books I kept

indicators.note: kept means the popular word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: something hot is extremely popular, much in demand
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for books

explanation.surface: A small creature appears in hugely popular books that I hung on to.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the creature is the hero of a very popular book.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's halflings are small humanlike beings, so a little creature.

clue.text: Carpenter's piece of furniture a lady accepted

definitions.note: read as Carpenter is: the title character is a carpenter

indicators.note: accepted means the lady phrase takes the furniture inside

parts.note: a dame is a lady, also a title
a bed is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A carpenter's bit of furniture was taken by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot's novel Adam Bede has a carpenter as its hero; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eponymous hero of George Eliot's first novel works as a village carpenter.

clue.text: Exhausted, filling in with one role in several pieces

indicators.note: the stale word is filled in with the other pieces inside it

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, exhausted by overuse
I is the Roman numeral one
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A tired actor fills in with a single part in a multi-act piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripartite means divided into three parts, so in several pieces.

clue.text: Come on, Americans! King is in trouble

parts.note: fans cheer 'Up the' team, meaning come on
the Cree are a Native American people
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to American supporters as their king faces difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the Rovers!' is a British football chant meaning 'come on, Rovers!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up the creek is an informal idiom for being in serious difficulty.

clue.text: How this bird gets late afternoon sun on back?

definitions.text: How this bird gets late afternoon sun on back?

parts.words: How this bird gets late afternoon sun on back?
parts.note: a wader that flips pebbles hunting food; read as two words, its back changes colour as it tans

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a shorebird named for flipping pebbles to find prey; split, it changes shade.

clue.text: Woman's right, as always

parts.note: Eve is the first woman, a stock name

explanation.surface: A woman insists she is right, as she always is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever is a synonym of always, as in for ever.

clue.text: Entrances fluffed, but coming up again

indicators.note: fluffed means bungled, so the letters come out wrong

explanation.surface: An actor fluffs entrances but bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn, reviving and coming into being again.

clue.text: My view is, enter revolutionary sort of church

indicators.note: enter means the view phrase goes inside the revolutionary word

parts.note: red is a revolutionary, a communist
for me means in my view

explanation.surface: Someone opines on joining a radical church.
explanation.definitionFit: Reformed churches are Protestant churches in the Calvinist tradition.

clue.text: Regret returning old currency

indicators.note: returning means the regret word is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone regrets coming back to a defunct currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old currency' reads as the definition, but the euro is current; 'old' only gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the money used across much of the European Union.

clue.text: Play first game of new campaign: anyone could be opposition here

definitions.text: Play first game of new campaign
definitions.meaning: literally, to start the sporting year with its first fixture
the idiom for a time when anyone may be freely attacked or targeted

explanation.surface: A team kicks off the season in a free-for-all where any side could face them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a period when attacks on anyone are allowed, or literally a season's start.

clue.text: In life, we struggle for what is most opposite

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Life is a struggle against the hardest opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most opposite' reads as 'most contrary', but means the opposite of 'most'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewest is the antonym of most when counting things.

clue.text: Picked up bad cut in centre

indicators.note: in places the cutting word inside the centre word

parts.note: mid means centre, as in midfield
to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone receives a poor haircut in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to catch words wrongly, so picked up badly by ear.

clue.text: Wizard comics seen round university

indicators.note: seen round means the comics word encircles the university

parts.note: comics are magazines, mags for short

explanation.surface: A wizard reads comics around campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a sorcerer or magician, as in the Magi of the Nativity.

clue.text: Works in college

definitions.meaning: a body of writings, the complete output of an author
... Christi is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge

explanation.definitionFit: A corpus is an author's complete works, and Corpus is short for Corpus Christi College.

clue.text: With smell overcoming resistance, one gets stuck into dinner

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming puts the smell word over and around the resistance letter

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A smelly dinner overpowers any reluctance to eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a tine of a fork, the part plunged into food at dinner.

clue.text: Dogs finally given docked tail

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

parts.note: a docked tail has been cut short

explanation.surface: Dogs have their tails docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Dictionary-maker to apologise humbly, having omitted line

indicators.note: having omitted means the line letter is dropped

parts.note: to grovel is to apologise abjectly

explanation.surface: A lexicographer has to say sorry abjectly, leaving out a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir George Grove compiled the famous Dictionary of Music and Musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Grove compiled a standard music dictionary still known by his name.

clue.text: Trouble as Whitehall warriors cut pay

indicators.note: cut means the pay word is split open by the ministry

parts.note: income is pay received
the MoD, Ministry of Defence, is the Whitehall department for the armed forces

explanation.surface: Defence officials cause problems by slashing wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode is a formal verb for inconveniencing or troubling someone.

clue.text: Cake courses in wrong order?

indicators.note: in wrong order puts the dessert course ahead of the main one

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert course
meat is the main course of a meal

explanation.surface: A diner is served cake with the courses mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: A meal runs meat then sweet; swapped, the two courses make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is a sweet delicacy such as a small cake or candied fruit.

clue.text: Need a bit of a hand to do this in garden?

definitions.meaning: a finger or thumb, part of the hand
read as two words, what you do to soil with a spade

explanation.surface: A gardener wants a helping hand with the digging.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a finger, part of a hand; split, the letters give a gardening command.
